newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson Breweries posts loss after Coors settlement.
newsitem.headline: Molson Breweries posts loss after Coors settlement.

text.p: Molson Breweries, Canada's largest beermaker, said on Tuesday it posted a net loss of C$184.6 million ($133.4 million) in the fourth quarter ended April 1, compared to a loss of C$79.1 million ($57.6 million) in the same period a year ago.
Molson said the bulk of its loss resulted from a C$100 million ($72.25 million) settlement with U.S.-based Adolph Coors Co related to Molson's licensing rights to Coors products in Canada.
For the full year, Molson reported a net loss of C$16.8 million ($12.1 million) compared to a net profit of C$75.8 million ($54.8 million) in fiscal 1996.
Molson is owned 40 percent each by Australian-based Fosters Brewing Group Ltd and Canada's Molson Cos Ltd, and 20 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc's Miller Brewing Co.
Also during the fourth quarter, Molson recorded a C$15 million ($11 million) charge related to other costs and a C$17 million ($12.3 million) provision for closing its Winnipeg brewery.
It also took C$33 million (US$24 million) in charges related to the rationalization of operations.

The brewer said it recorded a C$11.5 million ($8.3 million) charge for the early repayment of secured debt and a C$61 million ($44.1 million) provision for severance and costs related to its reorganization plan.

"It was a challenging year for Molson Breweries but most of the external issues, including the settlement of the Coors claim, are behind us and we can turn our attention more fully to completing the turnaround that started last year," John Barnett, President and Chief Executive Officer of Molson Breweries, said in a statement.

Molson said annual sales rose 1.4 percent to C$2.12 billion ($1.53 billion) in 1997 from C$2.09 billion ($1.51 billion last year. The sales improvement reflected the impact of price increases and the acquisition of several independent agents in Quebec.
"However, this increase was partially offset by lower domestic sales volume and reduced sales to the United States," Molson said.
Molson said exports to the U.S. were down 2.9 percent over the previous year, reflecting weakness in the ice beer segment in which Molson Ice was the leading brand.

Molson said its 46.1 percent share of all beer sold in Canada during the year compared to a 44.05 percent marketshare for arch-rival Labatt Brewing Co, which is owned by Belgian beer giant Interbrew S.A.
